senses.gloss: f. (κάλαθος, prob. of Semitic origin, v. preced.; v. Lewy, Sem. Fremdw. p. 109) vase-shaped basket, esp. woman’s work-basket.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 8:1">Gitt. VIII, 1</cite> <he>זרקו … לתוך קַלָּתָהּ</he> if he throws the letter of divorce into her lap or into her basket.
<cite ref="Gittin 78a:10">Ib. 78ᵃ</cite> <he>כל דבר שהוא כקלתה</he> any receptacle that is designated for her specific use like her basket.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 9b:8">B. Mets. 9ᵇ</cite> <he>ק׳ מינח נייחא וכ׳</he> (if he throws the document into her basket on her head,) her basket is at rest, but she moves under it.

<cite ref="Ketubot 72b:1">Keth. 72ᵇ</cite> top <he>ק׳ שפיר דמי</he> if she goes out with her basket on her head, it is right (she cannot be legally sued for indecent conduct); <he>דת יהודית אפי׳ ק׳ וכ׳</he> but so far as Jewish custom is concerned, it is improper to go out uncovered even with the basket on the head.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 8:1:5">Y. Gitt. VIII, beg. 49ᵇ</cite> <he>היתה ק׳ של זהב</he> if the basket (into which he threw the letter of divorce) was of gold; a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="S01433"><he>קַלָּתוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bikkurim 3:8">Bicc. III, 8</cite> <he>העשירים … בק׳ של וכ׳</he> the rich brought the first-fruits in baskets of silver or of gold. Gitt. l. c. <he>מוכר ק׳</he> a dealer in baskets.
